change: New Resilience product: landing page with live Akvan strip, India map that toggles between event and vulnerability views, and an event stub page
Resilience map gains a real groundwater stress layer from the CGWB 2024 state table, with a legend; per-stress captions and hash links
Resilience flood layer: district-level share of flooded area from the India Flood Inventory, drawn at district granularity with a legend and a no-data caveat
Resilience drought tab: live district drought (D2-D4 share) from the India Drought Monitor, joined by LGD code, with a Live/Historical toggle whose historical layer is pending
Historical drought layer built from the Drought Intelligence Explorer SPI-12 record, 1981-2025, 642 districts, behind the live/historical radio control
Akvan event map shows the observed track: earlier IMD positions as small dots joined by a solid line, forecast as the dashed line
Poller script for the Akvan page: interval guard, bulletin-time dedupe, sanity box, stop condition, marker block regenerated whole; README with cron and systemd recipes

Akvan event page carries the resource cards (emergency numbers, what to do, report a problem, relief, documents). Superseded in part by akvan-prepare-emergency, which split the first two into their own sections

While an event is live the site root opens the event page; ?site=1 or a session choice shows the main site, which the event strip links to prominently. The poller flips the redirect off when the event ends

Event page carries the storm map (cropped to the Bay of Bengal) and a slim strip with only the way back to the main site; the main site keeps the vulnerability map alone, with no Akvan tab; the poller now redraws the event page
Akvan page top row: map at half width on the left, a 2x2 of Position, Intensity, Track and Rainfall on the right; warnings and the rest below
Akvan right column: emergency strip with a link to the help section above a 2x2 of cards; strip plus two rows equal the map height, map stretches to the row

Akvan page order set: top row, then Timeline, help material, warnings, report, relief and documents. Later edits renamed the help and warnings sections and held relief back, so this entry records the order rather than the exact headings
Akvan final section reduced to a single Sources card; section headings in the region style with a bullet and larger mono caps

Prepare and be safe section with Before, During, After and the NDMA link in four cards; emergency numbers in their own full-width section as bordered rows (the section and the strip it describes were replaced when the event page was rebuilt)
Akvan: guidance card tinted to separate it from the three action cards, footer back link removed, relief section held back for now
Section renamed Warnings and advisories; the placeholder card now carries a paragraph so it takes the same type as every other card
Akvan page: the closing note under the sources removed, so the page ends with the sources card
The main-site pill and the emergency arrow circle are inverted: white fill, red mark, reverting on hover

Resilience landing page cleaned after the event tab moved out: event caption under the map removed, status card rewritten to describe the vulnerability map, hero mark swapped for the drawn one, source line corrected to 11:30

Akvan page and the main strip brought to IMD National Bulletin 5 (02:30 IST, 16 Nov): deep depression at 10.6N 86.7E at 23:30, moving 8 kmph, cyclone expected on the evening of the 16th, name not yet conferred (the section and the strip it describes were replaced when the event page was rebuilt)
Poller date parser accepts a comma between the month and the year, as in 15th November, 2026; without it an observation was dated to the wrong day
The Emergency information card on the event page takes a terracotta border instead of the hairline grey
Emergency information rows set a size larger and darker: 15.5px in near-black, with the numbers at 16px
Map script rewritten after the event tab was removed: it no longer touches the deleted tab and event nodes, so each stress chip now shows its own caption instead of leaving the cyclone one in place

The tricolour band under the hero on the resilience and event pages replaced by twin terracotta rules of the same 4px weight, with the grey between them taken out (the rules are now Mapunity green rather than terracotta)
The mark's box tightened to its ink, and the event page hero gained the mark the main page already had. The offset from the band was then reduced to the content edge (logo-to-card-edge)

The hero mark pulled back from the band's bleed to the content edge, so its ink lands on the right edge of the Emergency information card rather than running past it. The negative margin was trimmed when the mark was resized (hero-mark-size)

The hero mark set to 76px rather than 104px: the other marks are square lockups with their wordmark inside, so at 104 they read compact, while this is a bare portrait glyph whose ink fills the box and so read taller than them
The event page pointed at the mark one directory too high, so it broke in the tree as well as in the delivered copy; corrected to ../../logos/ and delivered through the inliner

The event title carries the system's designation BOB/10/2026 while it is unnamed, with the likely name beside it; the page title and the tab follow (superseded: the name was conferred at 17:30 on 16 November)
The poller rewrites the event title when IMD confers the name: BOB/10/2026 with its note becomes Cyclone Akvan, the page title follows, and the standfirst stays
Event page top row: the two rows of cards size to their own content instead of being forced equal, which brings the map card from 888 to 714 and leaves each row internally matched
The crumb above the event title reads Public AI, a dot, then Resilience

The published event page checks data/observations.json on load and every ten minutes, and redraws the marker, dots, track, label and Position card when the record carries a newer bulletin; the poller now writes that file beside events/ and parses the distance phrases into it

A post-event page for Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the south Andhra coast near Ongole on 3 November 2026: nine observed fixes on the map, how the warnings helped, the state damage assessment and what it left behind
A post-event page for Cyclone Arnab, which crossed near Yanam on 28 October 2026, the first of the two Andhra cyclones that week

One EVENTS card sits beside the map, its head on white with a terracotta hairline and a count, holding a row per storm: the live depression tagged and barred in terracotta, then Arnab and Murasu, each naming its peak category, dates and three worst-hit states

The pills sat high in their header row because the chips container still carried the old eight pixels of bottom padding. Cleared, the space above and below the pills is now 13 and 14 pixels, so they read as centred
The stress pills read Cyclones, Floods and Landslides, in the plural, alongside Drought, Heat and Groundwater
The map footer is a white band spanning the full width of the card, separated from the map by a hairline, with the card rounded corners kept; the El Nino page follows the same rule
The EVENTS label sits alone in the card head, two sizes larger and aligned to the right rather than the left

A SEASON card under EVENTS carries the standing ocean state: very strong El Nino, Nino-3.4 at +2.5 C, likely strong through January to March 2027, with the three effects that matter to this page, rain, heat and cyclones, and the sources named

Everything below the first row is gone from the landing page: the three explanatory cards, the two doors and the What a page carries row. The page is the map, the events and season cards, and the footer
The footer text and its light rule are gone; the page closes with the same twin terracotta band that opens it

A page for the very strong El Nino of 2026 to 2027, in the same shape as the storm pages: the three Nino indices as bars against the very-strong threshold, what it does to India, what to watch and the sources. It is listed as a live row in the EVENTS card, which replaces the separate Season card

The closing band no longer overflows the page: it was sitting outside the page container with a 24px negative margin on both sides, which pushed the document 24px wider than the window and produced a horizontal scrollbar at every width. It is now constrained to the same 1190px column as the opening band
The sources card on every resilience event page now runs the full width of the column, the same as the card above it. The single-column grid had been capped at 620px

The resilience mark pointed at logos/ inside the resilience folder, where there is no logos directory, so the header logo was broken in the tree. It now points at ../logos. A sweep of every page found eight more broken image paths, in one Bengaluru South asset page and seven archive pages, all now fixed

On the El Nino card the label and the view selector sit in a strip flush with the top of the card, level with the terracotta bar beside it, 44px deep with equal air above and below the pill. Then the data, then the caption inside the card

The caption on the El Nino card sits inside the card again: the box, the view and the caption are a flex column, so the caption takes its space first and the graph fills what is left, instead of the caption spilling over the row below
The caption on the El Nino card carries wider side padding, 26px against 14px, and the wording is shorter so it still fits in fewer lines. The map caption is trimmed to match

The graph in the El Nino card sits 20px below the strip instead of touching it, the dead air beneath it is gone, and the caption carries the fuller explanation again, so the space went into words rather than emptiness

The Akvan page carries the 08:30 fix of 16 November, 11.2N 86.4E, and the outlook has moved south: IMD now puts the crossing between Nellore and Tuni by noon on 20 November. The timeline, the position and intensity cards and the forecast line on the map all follow the bulletin

The note under the position cards said IMD observes only up to 17:30. It now says every three hours round the clock, 02:30 to 23:30, which is what the record itself shows: the 15 November fix at 23:30 came from one of those night bulletins

The record now keeps a rejected list beside the observations. One secondary report carries an 11:30 position for Akvan, but it puts the centre south-east of the 08:30 fix, against the stated north-north-west motion, so it is held there with the reason and not plotted. No 14:30 or 17:30 fix could be reached

The Akvan map card carries three views behind one selector: the forecast track, a true-colour frame from VIIRS on NOAA-20 for 16 November 2026, and the same pass in brightness temperature at 11.45 microns. Each view has its own caption and source. The frames are stored with the page and travel with it

Akvan was named at the 17:30 bulletin on 16 November, at 12.2N 85.7E as a cyclonic storm. The page is retitled Cyclone Akvan, the track now carries all eight fixes from 15 November, and the timeline, position and intensity cards follow the bulletin. The two missing fixes of the day, 05:30 and 11:30, are recorded too

The track is now kept as a record rather than a drawing: the poller appends every fix and never overwrites one, tools/export_track.py writes the record out as a CSV and reports any gap longer than four hours, and the README says why the earlier storms carry only a handful of points
The map and the satellite frames run to the top, left and right edges of the card, rounded with it, and keep their space only below, where the caption sits

Checked at 06:10 IST on 17 November: no 17 November fix had been published that could be verified, and NASA Worldview carries no 17 November pass over the Bay at that hour, so the marker and both satellite frames still show the 16th. The page now says when it was last checked and why the marker has not moved (superseded later the same morning, when the 05:30 bulletin appeared)

check.pattern: Last checked at 06:10 IST on 17 November

change: The first 17 November fix: 12.1N 85.8E at midnight, almost stationary, winds 62 kmph gusting 88 near the centre. It comes from Bangladesh Meteorological Department because IMD's own bulletin for the day was not reachable, and the page says so beside the position rather than passing it off as IMD's (the position card now carries the IMD 05:30 fix instead; the Bangladesh Met midnight fix stays in the record)

The map card has two views: the forecast track, and one satellite image. The image is an INSAT-3DS frame for 07:00 to 07:27 IST on 17 November, cropped to carry the whole Andhra and Odisha coast, and labelled simply Satellite with a plain caption. The channel choice is gone: two wavelengths were asking the reader a question the page does not need to pose

The 05:30 fix of 17 November: 12.2N 85.7E, unchanged from the previous evening, the centre practically stationary for twelve hours. The position and intensity cards say so, the track carries ten fixes, and the satellite frame is the 10:00 window from INSAT

The poller now refreshes the satellite frame as well as the position. tools/fetch_image.py fetches IMD's current INSAT image, checks the size, crops the Bay, writes it to data/satellite and restates the caption with the time we fetched it. The page stops claiming a scan window it cannot verify

Contrast raised across the resilience landing page without touching a font size or face: ink from #2b2620 to #1d1915, muted text from #6b635a to #453f37, the terracotta from #b05529 to #8f3d18, hairlines from 10 to 18 per cent black, and the map's district boundaries from #d9c9b4 to #b8a68e. The fills that encode exposure are unchanged

A second, deeper contrast pass on the resilience landing page. Ink to #0f0d0b, muted to #2b2721, terracotta to #772a0c, hairlines to 30 per cent black, the exposed states from a pale wash to #e2a382, the district boundaries to #8a7454. The smallest text, the dates, source lines and legend, now uses near-black rather than muted grey, since size cannot change

On the resilience landing page the event name is now black and the states it touched are in terracotta, with the name carrying the weight and the states reading as its caption. The reverse of what it was

In the EVENTS card the date now sits at the left of each row and the LIVE pill at the right, which separates the small dark date from the terracotta block. The closed events, which have no pill, put their dates at the left too, so every row starts the same way

The six stress pills now sit in a header row at the top of the map card, matching the EVENTS header: EXPOSURE in the same mono capitals at the left, the pills flowing right, a terracotta hairline beneath. The pills are a shade tighter so all six hold one line, and the map starts below the row

The two header rows are now the same height, 48 pixels, measured at top 205 and bottom 253 on both cards, so the EXPOSURE and EVENTS labels sit on one line and the two hairlines run level. The map card lost its 6 pixel padding so its header row bleeds to the card edge like the events one

The word EXPOSURE is gone from the map card's header row. The pills now start at the card's left edge, with the same 18 pixel inset as the EVENTS label opposite, and the row keeps its height and its hairline

The pills are no longer bunched at the left. They are spread across the header row with equal gaps, first pill flush with the card's left inset and last flush with its right, so the row reads as a single band (the pills later became tabs, still spanning the row)

The page now points at the satellite frame with a version query taken from the fetch time, so a browser cannot serve yesterday's cached copy after the file is replaced. tools/fetch_image.py writes it on every run

Refreshed at 12:35: the satellite frame is the 12:33 fetch from INSAT, and the 02:30 bulletin is now in the record, putting the centre at 12.2N 85.7E, the same point as 05:30. The note says the 11:30 bulletin carried no coordinates in anything reachable. Eleven fixes in the record
The live row in the EVENTS card is now Cyclone Akvan, dated since 15 November rather than a closed range, following the naming at 17:30 on the 16th

Written down in the resilience tools README: when IMD names a system, three files change together, the event page title, the live row on the index page and the named block in the record. The index row is the one that gets missed, because it is a different file from the one being edited

The naming rule now covers reclassification as well as naming. IMD changes the descriptor as the storm strengthens, cyclonic to severe to very severe, and the same three places must follow: event page title, the live row on the index page, and the intensity of each fix in the record

What an event is called now lives in one place, data/event.json: name, descriptor, status, dates and the states affected. tools/set_event.py rewrites the event page heading and the live row on the index page from it, and both pages also read the record at runtime, so an escalation is one command rather than two edits that can drift apart

Two things for posterity. tools/postevent.py keeps a per-cyclone record of what happened after the coast was crossed, deaths, shelters, crop, rain, each entry appended with its source and the time it was found. And fetch_image.py --keep saves a permanent copy of the satellite frame, so the picture at landfall survives IMD overwriting its own

The post-event routine now treats landfall as the start, not the end. Half the system is still at sea when the centre crosses, so the page stays live until the rear has cleared, that moment is logged with --cleared, three satellite frames are kept rather than one, and figures gathered before clearance are marked provisional because they will move

The six stress pills are now tabs. No background, no rounded box: mono capitals in the header row, the active one in terracotta with a three pixel rule sitting on the header hairline, the rest in dark ink. They still span the row
The tab labels are 11.5 pixels, two more than before, so they read as headings rather than captions. All six still hold one line and the row keeps its height

Landslides is off the resilience map. There is no district layer to show and the events are too sudden and local to sit under a resilience reading, so the tab, its caption block and its entry in the script's list of stresses are gone. Five tabs remain

Refreshed at 05:58 on the 18th: the frame is the 05:56 fetch, and the 20:30 bulletin of the 17th is in the record at 12.4N 85.6E, still a cyclonic storm. Fifteen fixes. No bulletin for the 18th had been published when the page was checked, and the page says so rather than moving the marker on a forecast

The Cyclones tab no longer shades whole states, which claimed an exposure the coast does not share. It plots the landfall point of every cyclone that crossed the Indian coast in the last five years: Tauktae, Yaas and Gulab in 2021; Mandous in 2022; Biparjoy and Michaung in 2023; Remal, Dana and Fengal in 2024; Montha in 2025; Arnab and Murasu in 2026. Twelve dots, each with the name and place on hover, and a caption that says why the dots are all on the coast

Two rings join the twelve dots on the Cyclones tab, for the storms that crossed outside India and still hurt India: Sitrang into Bangladesh in 2022, which flooded 83 villages and 325 hectares of crop in Assam and damaged houses in Mizoram, and Mocha into Myanmar in 2023, which damaged 236 houses and affected 5,749 people in Mizoram and brought heavy rain to Kolkata. The caption explains the two marks

The Cyclones tab now carries thirty-six seasons of landfalls, 1990 to 2026: forty cyclonic storms that crossed the Indian coast, coloured by decade in a four-step terracotta ramp, and two rings for Sitrang and Mocha, which crossed abroad and still reached Assam and Mizoram. A legend sits in open water off the east coast naming the four decades

The landfall layer gains a decade box on the map, so one decade can be read alone: 41 dots across four decades, 8 in the 1990s. Eight rings now mark crossings outside India that reached it, in Bangladesh in 1991, 1997, 2007, 2016, 2017 and 2022 and Sri Lanka in 2020, each in its decade colour. The land is white so the four colours separate, and the legend sits in open water off the east coast

The landfall layer is rebuilt from IMD's state tables and the state disaster registers instead of a hand list, which had left out fourteen events on the Andhra coast alone. It now carries 55 crossings on the Indian coast and 10 rings for crossings abroad, 65 in all, coloured by decade with the decade box and legend as before

The decade box and the legend are now one panel in the bottom right of the map: All decades, then the four decades as selectable rows, then a note row for the rings. Colours are pulled apart to black, red, orange and green so each decade is unmistakable, the labels are 12 pixels rather than 9, and the decade labels read 1990s rather than 1990S

The All decades row carries a swatch of its own, the four decade colours in one circle, and it shows as selected on load with the terracotta ring around it, so the default state of the panel is visible rather than implied

Each row of the landfall panel carries its count: 65 in all, 16 in the 1990s, 11 in the 2000s, 19 in the 2010s, 19 in the 2020s, and 10 outside India. The word crossed is gone, so the last row reads outside India

The circles are now sized by each storm's peak IMD category, from a depression at 3.4 pixels to a super cyclone at 8.8, so the strongest landfalls read heaviest: 17 very severe, 15 severe, 13 cyclonic, 4 extremely severe, 3 depressions, 1 deep depression and 2 super cyclones on the coast. The panel carries a compact size key

The landfall dots sat inland because the projection lost its scale on the vertical axis when the layer was rebuilt with sizes: the y term multiplied latitude by the longitude factor as well as the scale, compressing every point northwards by seven per cent. Corrected, the dots sit on the coast again, at the places their tooltips name
The word size is gone from the key and the phrase stronger storm is set at 12 pixels in ink rather than 9 in grey, so the three dots now read as a scale without a caption telling you what a scale is

A landfall the state tables did not carry: the December 1993 very severe cyclonic storm that came ashore near Karaikal, found in the season record for that year. Fifty-six on the coast now, seventeen in the 1990s

The 1990s are rebuilt from the season records, which list crossings the state tables do not: 15 more landfalls, among them southern Odisha in November 1990, Badudebpur in 1991, Machilipatnam in October 1994, three May depressions in 1995 at Cuddalore, Tuni and Sagar Island, Balasore in September 1995, Diu in June 1996, Ongole in October 1996, and Narsapur in 1998. The 1990s now carry 32 of the 81 points

The 2000s are rebuilt the same way, adding 17 crossings the state tables missed: Kakinada 2000, Sagar Island 2002, Balasore 2003, Puri and Porbandar and Kalingapatnam in 2004, five in 2005 including Paradip, Porbandar, Kolkata, Ongole and Vedaranyam, Puri and Gopalpur in 2006, and two in 2007. Nisha is corrected: it crossed north of Karaikal, not Cuddalore. The 2000s carry 28 now, and the map 98 points

The 2010s and 2020s are completed the same way: 15 more crossings in the 2010s, including Paradip and Bapatla in 2010, Balasore 2011, three in 2013, Puri and Puducherry in 2015, Digha and Karaikal in 2016, two in 2017, and the Odisha and Gujarat depressions of 2019; and 11 more in the 2020s, among them three deep depressions in 2022 at Digha, Chennai and Andhra, Ratnagiri and the Odisha coast in 2023, two in 2024 and two in 2025. Arnab's point is corrected to the recorded 16.45N 81.90E. The layer now carries 114 crossings and 10 rings, 124 points

The size key has left the landfall panel and stands on its own above Sikkim, in the empty north-east of the map, so the panel is shorter and no longer sits over the Odisha and Bengal coast where the densest run of dots is

The map caption no longer describes the rings, since the panel already does, and it no longer calls everything a cyclone: it reads Landfalls, 1990 to 2026, every cyclonic disturbance that came ashore from depressions to super cyclones, which is what the dots actually are

check.pattern: Every cyclonic disturbance that came ashore

change: The sentence about the dots running the length of the seaboard is gone, and the source line that followed it now sits in the caption at the same size and colour as the text above, rather than as small grey mono
The caption opens Landfalls since 1990 rather than naming an end year, and drops the season count, so neither has to be rewritten when the record grows

Refreshed at 09:02 on the 18th: the frame is the 08:59 fetch, and the 23:30 and 02:30 fixes are in the record at 12.5N and 12.6N, 85.6E, still crawling north at 3 kmph. Seventeen fixes. Myanmar's met service reports a severe cyclonic storm at 05:00; IMD's own bulletins had not said so in anything reachable, and the Intensity card says which source says what

The Emergency information section is back on the Akvan page. It had been lost in the rollback that cut the page down on the 16th, leaving the strip at the top pointing at an anchor that no longer existed. The block is restored from the v147 archive unchanged: seven numbers, the note on where they were checked, and the anchor the strip needs

The two views in the map card now say when each is true for: Track 02:30, Satellite 09:36. The image tool rewrites the satellite time on every fetch, so the reader can see which of the two is fresher without having to open both. The track stays the default, since it carries the forecast and the coast

IMD stamps regional station codes across its satellite frames, VSK, BWN, CAL and the rest, in orange. They have nothing to do with the weather and they clutter the map, so the fetch tool now strips them: it masks the orange, grows the mask over the antialiased edges and fills from the local median, which holds the land tone underneath. Zero orange pixels remain in the frame

Every rule and hairline in the resilience files now takes Mapunity's greens, sampled from the logo: the twin rules under the hero in #205800 and #60a000, the header-row hairlines, the active tab underline, the card edges and the strip on a live row. Text and the LIVE pills stay terracotta, so the lines are the only thing that changed colour

The first resilience-only archive, cut from the contents of the resilience folder rather than from a folder inside it, so extracting it at resilience.mapunity.com gives index.html at the root. Twenty-three files, 1.3 MB, and a manifest at tools/manifests/r001.json so the next release can be cut as a patch against this one

The resilience mark is now the old Mapunity icon: two arrows pressing inward on a bar between two brackets, which reads as pressure meeting a structure rather than as a cyclone. It is drawn in the project terracotta, #b05529, the colour the spiral used, and it replaces the spiral on all five resilience pages and on publicai's card
The mark sits 10 pixels lower in the hero and is a fifth larger, 125 pixels against 104, on the landing page and on all four event pages. Its foot now clears the green rules by 11 pixels
Fifteen pixels of dead space off the top of every resilience page: seven from the body padding and eight from the hero's own top padding, so the eyebrow now starts 31 pixels down rather than 46

The resilience hero now matches District Mocha's to the pixel: crumb at 40, title at 63, standfirst at 111, and the header closing at 157 in both. Getting there meant shortening the standfirst to one line, from What India is exposed to, what stands in the way, and what to do when it arrives to Exposure, what stands in the way, and what to do when it arrives, since the second line was the whole of the remaining difference

The landing page no longer hands itself over to the live event page. The redirect script is gone from the page and set_redirect is retired in the position tool, so the next event cannot switch it back on. A live event is still a row on the landing page and a card in the map's EVENTS panel, so it is found by choice rather than by ambush

The band at the top of the event pages is gone, along with its styles. It existed to get people out of the redirect, and there is no redirect to escape. The crumb and the mark now link home instead, quietly. The event hero therefore opens at the same height as the landing page. The event pages' twin rules were also still terracotta, missed by the earlier greening because they used a different hex; they now match the landing page in #205800 and #60a000

The event pages now measure exactly as the landing page: crumb at 40, title at 63, standfirst at 111, mark between 21 and 146, header closing at 157. Their header was still carrying the old 32 pixel top padding, which the earlier tightening had missed because those files held the rule in a different place

Refreshed at 11:30 on the 18th. The 05:30 fix puts Akvan at 12.7N 85.5E, and IMD has upgraded it to a severe cyclonic storm, so the descriptor follows. IMD has also scaled back the coast: 100 to 110 kmph gusting 120 at landfall between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on the 20th, where yesterday it said 120 to 130. Eighteen fixes in the record, and the satellite frame is the 11:29 fetch with the station codes stripped

The reclassification reaches the title, which now reads Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan on the event page, in the browser tab and on the landing page's live row, with severe since 05:30 on 18 November under it. The descriptor drives the title in set_event.py, so the next upgrade is one command; I had edited the record by hand and skipped the tool, which is why the page still said Cyclone

The mark in the hero is a link home on all five pages: to ../index.html from the four event pages and to index.html from the landing page itself. The event pages had it since the band came off; the landing page did not. It is the only route back now that the band is gone

Checked all five pages for a District Mocha footer and there is none: no footer element, no shared footer script. What remained was the dead CSS that used to style one, four rules across the pages, and those are gone. The pages end on the band, which is all they carry

The second resilience-only archive, r002, carrying everything since r001: the arrows mark in terracotta and linked home, the hero matched to District Mocha's measurements, the green rules on the event pages, no auto-switch, no top band, no footer, and this morning's Akvan work through the 05:30 fix and the severe upgrade. Twenty-five files, 1.3 MB, with its manifest inside

The label rules for the event maps are applied again on Arnab, Murasu and Akvan: months in mixed case, Oct rather than OCT; sizes a shade smaller; every label kept off the track line and inside the map frame; the landfall label beside its point with the place under it. Arnab and Murasu also lose a stray label that had been sitting on the left edge, and Murasu's second of November is cut to a date alone since the card carries the detail
In Murasu the 31 Oct label sits to the right of its point, eight pixels clear of it and level with the dot, rather than below and to the left where it lay across the empty sea
Murasu labels nudged: the 31 Oct label another four pixels right of its point, and 2 Nov four pixels down

The Arnab labels were in the same face and weights as Murasu's but drawn a quarter larger on screen, because the two maps have different viewBox widths, 268 against 337, and both fill the same card. Arnab's label type is scaled by 268/337 so the two read at the same size: 7.6, 8.4 and 7.2 in the drawing, which is 9.5, 10.5 and 9 once the map is scaled to the page

Arnab runs almost due east to west, so a label beside a point lies along the track and crowds the dots. The labels now sit above and below the line in turn: 27 Oct above, the landfall line and near Yanam below the western end, 26 Oct named below the eastern end. The long place line is cut to near Yanam, since the crossing window is in the landfall card. The rule itself is written into the tools README, with the note about scaling type by viewBox width

Arnab: the landfall line moves five pixels up and five left, and the 26 Oct label moves right and breaks into two lines, 26 Oct over named. It went thirty pixels rather than fifty because the drawing ends at 546 and the label is right-anchored, so another twenty would have run off the frame

On the Arnab map the date now sits under the word LANDFALL rather than beside it, and the three lines LANDFALL, 28 Oct, near Yanam are set twelve drawing units apart, the same tight step the 26 Oct and named pair uses
The 26 Oct label on the Arnab map moves ten pixels left, off the frame edge and clear of the last dot

The first resilience patch, r002 to r003, for the copy Sridhar has. Four files: the three event pages carrying the label work, and the tools README with the labelling rule. 253 KB against 1.3 MB for a full archive. Applied to a clean r002 it reproduces the current tree exactly, which I checked by hash

The resilience project gets the same machinery as District Mocha: its own changelog and verifier at the site root, an archive kept outside the tree, a package tool that cuts a full archive or a patch from a named base, and a manifest per release. The history of these pages, 132 entries, moves out of the suite changelog into this one

The two Akvan cron jobs are deleted: the hourly poller and the daily post-event job. They had been pointed at resilience/ inside the District Mocha suite, which no longer exists, and each run was leaving a chat session behind in the account. The README now says how to switch scheduled updates back on against this site root, and what they cost

Refreshed at 16:00 on the 18th. The 11:30 fix puts Akvan at 13.1N 85.4E, moving north-north-west at 8 kmph where it had been crawling at 3. Two forecast changes: the crossing widens to Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh to Puri in Odisha, and the expected wind at the coast is cut again to 90 to 100 kmph gusting 110, from 100 to 110 this morning and 120 to 130 on the 17th. Red message warning for north Andhra, Yanam and south Odisha. Nineteen fixes; the frame is the 15:56 fetch. The fingerprint moved from the page, which now carries the 14:30 position, to the record, which keeps the 11:30 fix

Release r004, cut as a patch from r002, which is the copy Sridhar has, with the full archive beside it. Thirteen files: the three event pages with the label work, the changelog and its verifier and package tools, the record and its track export, and this afternoon's satellite frame and Akvan fix. Applied to a clean r002 it reproduces the tree exactly

The 08:30 fix is in at 12.9N 85.4E, which closes the gap between the 05:30 and 11:30 positions. Twenty fixes. The Intensity card now carries IMD's own expectation that the storm will not strengthen further, from the director general's briefing, alongside the 90 to 100 kmph coast forecast. Frame refreshed at 16:31

check.pattern: does not expect it to strengthen

change: The packager gains a check: it compares the folder against a release manifest both ways and names files that are new or resurrected and files that are in the release but gone from the folder. It runs quietly before every full or patch, so a file brought back by an older archive is seen before it reaches a commit. Tested by planting a file and watching it appear

Refreshed at 18:33. The 14:30 fix puts Akvan at 13.3N 85.3E, still a severe cyclonic storm, moving north-north-west at 8 kmph. Nothing in the bulletin changes the cards: no reclassification, and the crossing stays between Narsapur and Puri around noon on the 20th at 90 to 100 kmph gusting 110, so the Intensity and Track cards are left as they were. Twenty-one fixes; the frame is the 18:33 fetch. The footnote under the cards was still reading seventeen fixes and a 09:02 check, so it now reads twenty-one and 18:33. The 11:30 entry's fingerprint pointed at the position line, which this redraw replaced, so it now tests the record instead

Manual check at 23:25. The 17:30 and 20:00 bulletins exist but neither states a latitude and longitude in anything reachable, so the record stops at the 14:30 fix rather than carrying an inferred position. The note on the record now says so, and says that the 19:30 and 20:30 scheduled runs left no trace of having looked

A frame at 23:31, the first since the 18:33 one. The 19:30 and 20:30 runs fetched nothing at all, so the page had been showing a five-hour-old picture, which is the clearest sign yet that those two runs did nothing rather than finding nothing

Scheduled 02:00 run. The 17:30 and 20:30 fixes of 18 November both state a latitude and longitude, so both are now in the record: 13.6N 85.3E and 13.8N 85.3E, still a severe cyclonic storm, moving north-north-west at 9 kmph and then north at 10 kmph. Twenty-three fixes, the marker and track redrawn, the Track tab time, the position line and the footnote now reading 20:30 and twenty-three. The 23:30 bulletin of 18 November was not reachable, so the record stops at 20:30 rather than carrying the 14.1N 85.0E from the forecast table. Three fingerprints in the changelog went stale the moment the record moved on: the 14:30 entry pointed at the position line this redraw replaced, so it now tests the record; the 23:31 frame entry pointed at latest.json, which every fetch overwrites, so it now tests that the frame file itself survives; and the 23:25 manual note, which said the 17:30 bulletin gave no coordinates, is marked superseded, because the 17:30 fix has since been found with coordinates. Its fingerprint pointed at the position line this later run replaced, so it now tests the record

Scheduled 04:00 run. The 23:30 bulletin of 18 November is in, at 13.9N 85.3E, still a severe cyclonic storm and now moving north at 5 kmph: it came from IMD's ACWC Chennai coastal bulletin, whose synoptic situation is the 1800 UTC observation. Twenty-four fixes, the marker and track redrawn, the Track tab time, the position line and the footnote now reading 23:30 and twenty-four. The 02:30 bulletin of 19 November was not reachable at 04:09, and the 15.0N 85.6E in the JTWC and WMO tables and the 13.9N 84.8E in the weather.lk table are forecast positions, so neither is recorded. No reclassification, so the Intensity card and the descriptor are untouched. The 02:00 entry's fingerprint pointed at the position line this redraw replaced, so it now tests the record. The 02:00 entry had also never been written into CHANGELOG.md, which this run puts right alongside its own row

The station codes were never actually being stripped. The function existed but the save path wrote the crop straight out, and yesterday's frames looked clean only because the daytime product carries no codes at all. The night infrared frame does, which is why they came back at 04:09. The strip is now applied to the cropped frame before it is saved, the same cleaned frame is used for the kept copy, and the tool counts what is left afterwards and prints it

check.pattern: station codes left in the frame

change: Scheduled 06:00 run. No new fix: the 02:30 and 05:30 bulletins of 19 November were not reachable at 06:10 from any source, the RSMC coastal page, IMD's mirrored posts, the NOAA raw bulletin and the ACWC Chennai coastal bulletin all still serving the 1730 text of 18 November, and the 19 November press reports quoting only the 1730 and 2330 text. So the record stands at twenty-four fixes ending 13.9N 85.3E at 23:30, nothing was redrawn, and the Intensity and Track cards and the descriptor are untouched. The Bangladesh met service's 19 November bulletin gives only distances from Payra, Chittagong, Cox's Bazar and Mongla and no coordinates, so it carries no fix, and the 15.0N 85.6E in the JTWC and WMO tables is a forecast position. Landfall is forecast for noon on 20 November and has not begun, so no permanent frame was kept. The frame is the 06:03 fetch, with no station codes left in it

A live event page opens on the satellite frame rather than the track, since the frame is usually the more current of the two. The footnote is set from whichever view is checked rather than assuming the track, so the caption cannot contradict the picture

The Satellite tab time had stopped following the frame. The pattern that rewrites it expected the radio input with no attributes between value="sat" and the closing bracket, but the satellite view is now the checked one, so the tag reads value="sat" checked and the substitution silently matched nothing. The caption and latest.json moved on with each fetch while the tab stayed at 06:03. The pattern now allows attributes there, and this run set the tab to the 08:05 frame by hand

Scheduled 08:00 run. No new fix. National Bulletin No. 27, issued at 02:30 on 19 November, quotes the 2330 position of 18 November at 13.9N 85.3E and states no latitude and longitude for 02:30 itself, and the 05:30 bulletin was still not reachable at 08:10: IMD's coastal and sea-area pages, the RSMC coastal bulletin and IMD's mirrored posts all serve the 2330 or 1730 text of 18 November. Sakshi's 07:13 report carries APSDMA distances of 470 km to Narsapur, 490 to Kalingapatnam, 570 to Chennai, 580 to Gopalpur and 640 to Puri, shorter than the 2330 distances and so implying a newer centre, but it gives no coordinates and a distance is not a position. The record therefore stands at twenty-four fixes ending 13.9N 85.3E at 23:30, nothing was redrawn, the Intensity and Track cards and the descriptor are untouched, and the 14.0N 83.9E and 15.3N 85.9E in the forecast tables are not recorded. Landfall is forecast for noon on 20 November and has not begun, so no permanent frame was kept. The frame is the 08:05 fetch, with no station codes left in it
The crumb on the four event pages reads Resilience alone, not Public AI and Resilience. The pages sit inside the resilience site now, so naming its parent above it says nothing a reader needs

The white squares were IMD's own station markers, one beside each code, so removing the text left them standing as holes. They are now removed as well: the tool finds small blobs much brighter than their surroundings, which is what separates a marker from cloud, fills them from the local median, and leaves the state boundaries and the graticule alone. Checked on the frame by eye, not just by count
The landing page crumb reads Mapunity rather than Public A.I. The site now stands on its own address, so the name above it is the organisation, not the project it grew out of

Scheduled 10:00 run. The 05:30 fix of 19 November is in, at 14.5N 85.3E, severe cyclonic storm, northwards at 12 kmph. The 08:00 run had left it out because the bulletin was not reachable then; it is now carried verbatim by IMD's own post and by three outlets, while IMD's own PDF endpoints still serve the 02:30 text. The marker, dots, track, Track tab time, position footer and timeline card moved to 05:30. No 08:30 bulletin with a stated position had appeared by 10:10, and the intensity is unchanged, so no reclassification and no landfall frame

Scheduled 12:00 run. Two fixes added: 02:30 IST 19 November at 14.1N 85.3E (northwards at 5 kmph) and 08:30 IST at 14.9N 85.3E (northwards at 15 kmph), both stated with latitude and longitude in the bulletin text. The marker, dots, track, Track tab time and position footer moved to 08:30. The Track card now carries IMD's latest crossing line, between Narsapur and Puri close to the east of Gopalpur by noon of 20 November, and the Intensity card notes that the 08:30 bulletin repeats 90 to 100 kmph gusting 110. The category is unchanged, so set_event was not run, and landfall has not begun, so no permanent frame was kept

The dashed forecast line no longer ends at a fixed point near the central Andhra coast, which is where it had been anchored since the first day and why it kept pointing at a landfall IMD had already moved away from. The crossing corridor now lives in the record, Narsapur to Puri, and the map draws it as a bar along the coast with the dashed line running to its middle. Move the corridor in data/observations.json and the map follows

The page redraws the marker from data/observations.json when it loads, and that runtime copy of the drawing carried its own hard-coded forecast anchor at 302,576, so even a fresh build put the old line back in the browser. It now takes the corridor from the record it just fetched and draws the bar as well. The event record fetch also pointed at the old nested path and could never have resolved

A _headers file tells Netlify not to cache the HTML or the record. The page fetches the record with no-store and redraws itself, so a cached page gave the worst of both: a fresh position inside stale drawing code, which is why the marker moved to the 11:30 fix while the forecast line stayed on the old coast

Scheduled 16:00 run. The 11:30 IST fix of 19 November is in, at 15.4N 85.2E, severe cyclonic storm, northwards at 17 kmph, 430 km south of Gopalpur and 390 km east-southeast of Narsapur, with the latitude and longitude stated in the bulletin text. The marker, dots, track, Track tab time, position footer and timeline card moved to 11:30. The Track card now carries the 11:30 crossing line, between Narsapur and Puri close to Gopalpur by noon of 20 November, and the Intensity card notes that both the 08:30 and 11:30 bulletins repeat 90 to 100 kmph gusting 110. The category is unchanged, so set_event was not run, and landfall has not begun, so no permanent frame was kept

The corridor is now four points along the coast, Narsapur, Kalingapatnam, Gopalpur and Puri, and the bar is drawn through them, so it sits on the shoreline instead of cutting inland on a straight chord between the two ends. The dashed line ends at the named target, Gopalpur, where IMD says the centre passes closest, rather than at the chord's midpoint. Both the build and the runtime redraw do the same

Scheduled 18:00 run. IMD's 0900 UTC satellite fix bulletin of 19 November (= 14:30 IST) states the low-level centre at 15.4N 85.4E, T3.0 on INSAT-3DS, with the deep convection sheared to the north of the centre; that fix is appended to the record and the marker, dots, track, Track tab time, position line and timeline card moved to 14:30. The 14:30 national bulletin is based on the 1130 IST fix already recorded, so it added no position. Category unchanged (severe cyclonic storm, 90 to 100 kmph gusting 110), crossing still between Narsapur and Puri close to Gopalpur by noon of 20 November, so the Intensity and Track cards stand and set_event was not run. Centre about 430 km south of Gopalpur: no landfall, so no permanent frame was kept

The cache rules now cover every path. They were written as /*.html, which does not match an extensionless URL, and Netlify caches /events/akvan separately from the file it rewrites to: that address was serving a build from 12:10 while /events/akvan.html was current

Scheduled 20:00 run. No fix was added: no bulletin at 17:30 IST or later carried a stated latitude and longitude by 20:08 IST, and the 1430 IST slot in the record is already held by the satellite fix of 15.4N 85.4E, which is not overwritten. The 20:08 satellite frame replaces the 18:04 one and the Satellite tab time moves with it; the record, the map, the track and the cards are unchanged, still a severe cyclonic storm about 410 km south of Gopalpur with landfall expected near Gopalpur around noon on 20 November

The time on the Track tab now comes from the newest fix in the record, set by the same script that redraws the marker, rather than from whichever run last redrew the page. After the 20:00 run the tab read 11:30 while the marker said 14:30, because a run that adds no fix does not redraw

The Position card was blank of description because the newest fix, the 14:30 satellite fix, states a position and nothing else. Where a fix carries no distances, the card now falls back to the last bulletin that did and says which one it was, rather than leaving the sentence half written

The 17:30 IST fix of 19 November is in the record: 16.1N 85.2E, from IMD's ACWC Chennai bulletin issued 20:30 IST (1200 UTC). The Track card now carries the 17:30 bulletin's 350 km south of Gopalpur and 13 kmph, and the footer's last-checked time and fix count were brought up to date

The static time on the Track tab never moved off 11:30 because the redraw matched value="track" checked, and the satellite frame is the checked view. The pattern now matches the attribute list however it reads, so the published markup agrees with the marker before the script runs

The 20:30 IST fix of 19 November is in the record: 16.6N 85.2E, from IMD's ACWC Kolkata sea-area bulletin valid 18 UTC, which puts the centre 300 km south of Gopalpur and closing at 18 kmph. The Intensity and Track cards now carry that bulletin's weaker landfall: a cyclonic storm with 70 to 80 kmph gusting 90, crossing during the forenoon and afternoon of the 20th. The footer's last-checked time and fix count were brought up to date

The 23:30 IST fix of 19 November is in the record: 17.1N 85.1E, from IMD's ACWC Kolkata sea-area bulletin valid 21 UTC (the ACWC Chennai coastal bulletin issued 02:30 IST is based on the same 1800 UTC position), severe cyclonic storm, north-north-west at 19 kmph, 170 km south-east of Kalingapatnam and 240 km south of Gopalpur. The Track card now carries 240 km south of Gopalpur and 19 kmph in place of 300 km and 18; the timeline card gains the 23:30 position; the footer's last-checked time and fix count were brought up to date. Intensity card unchanged: the 23:30 bulletin repeats the 70 to 80 kmph gusting 90 crossing, so it does not move

The 02:30 IST fix of 20 November is in the record: 17.7N 84.9E, from IMD's National Bulletin No. 36 issued 05:30 IST (the CWC Visakhapatnam special bulletin based on 2100 UTC of the 19th carries the same position), and IMD records that the system weakened into a cyclonic storm there. set_event.py was run with the new descriptor, so the event page and the index live row read Cyclone Akvan and the header note dates the severe phase 05:30 on 18 November to 02:30 on 20 November. The Intensity card now gives 80 to 90 kmph gusting 100 at the fix and 70 to 80 gusting 90 at the coast; the Track card has the centre 170 km south of Gopalpur closing at 21 kmph, the crossing brought forward to the forenoon, and land interaction begun with the centre still at sea. Footer to 06:15 and thirty-three fixes
